newsitem.title: USA: Dime sees earnings boost from payment.
newsitem.headline: Dime sees earnings boost from payment.

text.p: Dime Bancorp Inc said Monday the federally-mandated special assessment of $26.3 million to recapitalize the Savings Association Insurance Fund, which cut its third quarter net $15.2 million, or $0.14 per share, is expected to result in annual after-tax savings of $5 million, or $0.05 per share, starting in 1997.

"We strongly supported the BIF-SAIF legislation, were pleased that it was passed this year, and believe that the final result provides a fair solution for all concerned," Dime said. "Importantly, it helps preserve the competitiveness of the Dime franchise going forward."

"The 1996 third quarter results also included $11.4 million of losses on the sale of approximately $300 million of relatively low-yielding mortgage-backed securities. The proceeds of these sales are being re-invested in higher-yielding assets -- principally, loans.

"These sales are part of an ongoing capital management strategy intended to reduce our reliance on wholesale activities, as well as to improve our margin and our interest rate risk profile," Dime said.

"Excluding the after-tax effect of the unusual events in 1996 and merger-related expenses incurred in 1995, our 1996 third quarter earnings were $30.7 million, up 51 percent from $20.4 million in the third quarter of 1995 and up six percent from the 1996 second quarter earnings of $29.0 million," Dime said.

"The third quarter produced another solid performance for our core businesses. Deposits grew $73 million during the quarter; the loan portfolio increased $363 million; the margin widened five basis points; asset quality improved; and fee income was up. We also maintained our emphasis on controlling expenses." -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610
